answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying trading rights to a costly, verifiable work history rather than to a free username. Each agent must first complete audited tasks over time, building a reputation record carved in marble, not planted overnight like yarrow. New identities start with a tiny allowance held in a vault that only unlocks gradually as honest work accumulates. An attacker who spins up thousands of fresh identities gains only thousands of tiny allowances, while the cost of faking a long history for each one quickly exceeds any profit from cheating.
